title: glmtree
text: R package PhD thesis: logistic regression trees (tree whose leaves hold logistic regressions) fitted stochastic EM (SEM) algorithm. Entry point: glmtree() R/glmtree.R. S4 class glmtree. Sister package: ../glmdisc (conventions).

title: glmtree
text: Key design points (read changing SEM loop): - Segments integer labels kept whole chain (never recoded / refactored). c_hat sampled segment, c_map tree’s probable segment; criterion iteration computed c_map tree iteration - 1 (one produced ), pair stored “best”. - Logistic regressions glm.fit design matrix built ; aliased coefficients set 0; prediction coefficient lookup (best.tree$coefficients). glm objects best.tree$glms inspection fitted design columns. - Held-sets: validation used select iteration, test report performance best tree. Unseen factor levels prediction time get positive rate segment. - S4 class name glmtree clashes S3 class partykit::glmtree() (MOB) objects: predict / print methods must hand non-S4 objects callNextMethod() package must register S3 predict.glmtree (override partykit’s). Tested. - BIC segment uses log(segment size); kept original code purpose, flag changing. - ctree ~70% runtime; speed ups rest done (see NEWS / benchmarks).

title: Logistic regression trees with glmtree
text: "tree" scenario sign effect x2 x3 depends categorical feature x1 (six levels come three pairs), single logistic regression misspecified. predict() gives probability positive class (, type = "segment", segment) new observations; fitted tree fit@best.tree$tree (partykit object can plotted) logistic regression segment fit@best.tree$glms.  evolution criterion along chain (BIC, computed training set, higher better) shows chain settles; iterations burn-can selected.  compare test-set Gini index (2 AUC - 1) single logistic regression partykit::glmtree() (model-based recursive partitioning, MOB), looks splits parameter instability test instead likelihood-based latent variable.
code: data <- generateData(n = 2000, scenario = "tree") train <- sample(nrow(data), 1400) features <- c("x1", "x2", "x3") fit <- glmtree(   x = data[train, features], y = data$y[train],   K = 5, iterations = 100,   ctree_controls = partykit::ctree_control(alpha = 0.1, minbucket = 80, maxdepth = 4) ) fit #> Logistic regression tree fitted by SEM #>   segments: 3 | best iteration: 35 of 100  #>   bic of the best tree: -1463 (training set) #>  #> Model formula: #> .segment ~ x1 + x2 + x3 #>  #> Fitted party: #> [1] root #> |   [2] x1 in 1, 2, 3, 4 #> |   |   [3] x3 <= 0.49388: 3 (n = 583, err = 47.7%) #> |   |   [4] x3 > 0.49388: 4 (n = 359, err = 62.1%) #> |   [5] x1 in 5, 6 #> |   |   [6] x1 in 5 #> |   |   |   [7] x2 <= 0.55806: 5 (n = 151, err = 1.3%) #> |   |   |   [8] x2 > 0.55806: 5 (n = 85, err = 56.5%) #> |   |   [9] x1 in 6 #> |   |   |   [10] x2 <= -0.33494: 5 (n = 96, err = 47.9%) #> |   |   |   [11] x2 > -0.33494: 5 (n = 126, err = 29.4%) #>  #> Number of inner nodes:    5 #> Number of terminal nodes: 6 table(true_cluster = data$c[-train], segment = predict(fit, data[-train, features], type = "segment")) #>             segment #> true_cluster   3   4   5 #>            1 127  68   0 #>            2 130  65   0 #>            3   0   0 210 plot(fit@best.tree$tree) plot(unlist(fit@performance$criterionEvolution), type = "l", xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "-BIC") abline(v = fit@performance$best_iteration, lty = 2) logit <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = data[train, ], family = binomial) mob <- partykit::glmtree(y ~ x2 + x3 | x1 + x2 + x3, data = data[train, ], family = binomial) c(   logit = normalizedGini(data$y[-train], predict(logit, data[-train, ], type = "response")),   mob = normalizedGini(data$y[-train], predict(mob, data[-train, ], type = "response")),   glmtree = normalizedGini(data$y[-train], predict(fit, data[-train, features])) ) #>     logit       mob   glmtree  #> 0.1917357 0.6472518 0.6169301

code: data <- generateData(n = 2000, scenario = "tree") train <- sample(nrow(data), 1400) mixed <- FactoMineR::FAMD(data[train, features], graph = FALSE) cluster <- function(newdata) stats::predict(mixed, newdata)$coord[, "Dim 1"] < 0 segment <- cluster(data[, features]) pred <- numeric(nrow(data)) for (j in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {   model <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = data[train, ][segment[train] == j, ], family = binomial)   pred[segment == j] <- predict(model, data[segment == j, ], type = "response") } normalizedGini(data$y[-train], pred[-train]) #> [1] 0.4744621

title: Logistic Regression Trees
text: numbers come inst/benchmarks/real_data.R (20 random stratified 70/30 splits per dataset, 100 SEM iterations, K = 5; full table raw results inst/benchmarks/results/). test-set Gini coefficients (2 AUC - 1, higher better), means splits. Tree-based methods use leaves least 5% training data depth 4. glmtree selects tree BIC training data, glmtree (valid.) uses 25% training data validation set Gini. MOB partykit::glmtree(), model-based recursive partitioning, features regressors partitioning variables. says, honestly: glmtree general-purpose accuracy booster. helps population really made segments different regressions: simulation three segments goes 0.248 (one logistic regression) 0.650, using 4.1 segments average (three true). five real datasets single-tree method (ctree, MOB, glmtree) beats plain logistic regression: glmtree 0.002 0.038 , data close single regression chain mostly keeps one two segments (1.2 1.7 average). random forest ahead, German credit (+0.027 ± 0.007, paired mean ± standard error) CreditCard (+0.022 ± 0.006). partykit::glmtree() (MOB) stronger faster alternative data. simulation segments MOB scores higher glmtree (0.698 0.650) takes 1.4 s per fit 11 s. real data sets MOB either split (identical logit: Pima, Default, Caravan) loses (German credit 0.436, CreditCard 0.654), glmtree stays close logit. glmtree neither faster accurate MOB benchmark; offers different, likelihood-based search (latent segment variable), choice criterion (BIC, AIC, held-Gini) ctree segmentation. validation set version worse choice small samples (German credit 0.393, Pima 0.633): holding data makes fit selection noisy. Prefer BIC training data unless sample large. Cost. fit 100 iterations takes 3 18 s data sets (5 s 1319 observations, 18 s 7000 training observations; 160 s 85 features Caravan), measured six fits running parallel. 70% time spent partykit::ctree, refitted every iteration. Compared package’s version 0.3.1, rewrite version 0.4.0 made iteration twice fast accuracy (2.4×, 2.2× 2.0× 1000, 3000 10000 observations, 50 iterations; inst/benchmarks/speed.R). Convergence slow iterations. simulation segments, test Gini rises iteration budget (BIC training data, mean 12 repetitions): 0.639 (25 iterations), 0.645 (50), 0.652 (100), 0.658 (200), 0.664 (400), 0.676 (800), best iteration still far chain (349 average 800). patience = 25 chain stops 51 iterations 5 s Gini 0.646, 75 s 800 iterations: use patience quick answer, large iterations extra 0.03 Gini matters (inst/benchmarks/convergence.R). Reproduce Rscript inst/benchmarks/real_data.R 20 100 Rscript inst/benchmarks/convergence.R (need partykit, ranger, scorecard, ISLR, AER; hour).

text: test validation now documentation says. now held sets drawn never used: regressions, trees criteria computed observations. training set now data used fit; validation selects iteration; test used report performance best tree (performance$performance). validation versions criteria broken version 0.3.1: criterion = "aic" validation = TRUE failed “factor x1 new levels”, BIC returned -Inf, Gini mixed labels validation observations predictions one segment. now computed correctly (log-likelihood Gini held set). title: glmtree 0.4.0
text: SEM loop rewritten: one glm.fit per segment design matrix built instead glm() + predict() whole data frame segment iteration, single prediction tree per iteration instead two, vectorized sampling segments instead apply(sample()) rows. See inst/benchmarks/speed.R timings. Dependencies reduced partykit (dplyr, magrittr caret longer needed); FactoMineR used optional vignette chunk. Defaults documented: test = FALSE, validation = FALSE, criterion = "bic". generateData() vectorized (distributions, different random stream). CI: standard r-lib/actions workflows (check Linux, macOS Windows plus job without suggested packages, coverage, styler, pkgdown) replace previous single workflow; renv, Travis committed docs/ removed. Added inst/benchmarks/, comparison logistic regression, ctree, model-based recursive partitioning random forest simulated real data.
